To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Carl Thompson <carl.thompson@DataForge.com>

Subject: On‑prem VPC fabric — service‑layer overlay validation & rollback plan

Hi all,

Following our architecture sync, I want to circulate the service‑layer overlay diagram (attached) and a proposed canary + rollback runbook ahead of the staging cutover next week. Key asks:

- Please review the overlay for control/data plane separation (especially the proxy‑sidecar routing and the NVA fallthrough).
- Confirm MTU assumptions for the GRE/VXLAN tunnels (we hit a few jumbo MTU edge cases in our lab; MTU test results attached).
- Provide explicit rollback criteria and a single point of contact (SPOC) for the canary window.

Attachments: fabric-service-overlay-diagram-v2.pdf (diagram), canary-rollback-runbook.md (draft), mtu-test-results-20260728.csv

High‑level plan in the runbook:
1) Canary on two tenant slices in staging (12:00–14:00 PDT)
2) Validate token routing and KV cache persistence for warm restarts
3) Monitor latency percentiles (p50/p95) and error budget burn; abort on >20% p95 regression or repeated 504s
4) If abort condition met -> immediate rollback to previous overlay and route shift to controlplane‑edge1

Carl — tagging you for DataForge NVA compatibility notes and any ACL caveats.

Thanks,
Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Senior PM, Deployments
Redwood Inference
From: Carl Thompson <carl.thompson@DataForge.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@datagrid.io, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 11:13:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On‑prem VPC fabric — service‑layer overlay validation & rollback plan

Tessa — thanks for the note and the artifacts. Quick run‑through from our side: 

- The overlay diagram looks good; DataForge NVAs will preserve DSCP but we saw path MTU discovery issues with VXLAN + jumbo frames on one vendor switch model. Recommend forcing MSS clamp on the tunnel endpoints (we can share config).
- ACLs: need an explicit exception for intra‑cluster health probes from 10.240.0.0/18 -> controlplane proxies. Our default deny will drop those without the rule.
- Fallback: we can accelerate a route fallback to your controlplane‑edge1 if you can advertise a shorter path (we tested that in our lab).

I'll attach a short config snippet for MSS clamp and the health‑probe ACL in a follow up. For the canary, my SPOC will be me (carl.thompson@DataForge.com) + ops@datagrid.io on standby.

—Carl
DataForge — Principal Network Eng
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Carl Thompson <carl.thompson@DataForge.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On‑prem VPC fabric — service‑layer overlay validation & rollback plan

Thanks Carl — that MSS clamp call is important. A few engineering notes / acceptance criteria I want to capture here: 

Acceptance criteria for canary success:
- KV cache warm restarts complete within 4s for cold miss window < 15s
- No client‑observed request path length increase > 3 hops post overlay (we'll validate via traceroute + span tags)
- p50/p95 token lookup latency within 10% of baseline for 30m window

Canary steps (more detail):
A) Pre‑canary checks (T‑2h): run mtu sweep (script attached), verify NVA MSS clamp pushed, verify ACL exception is present
B) Canary wave 1 (T+0): shift 5% of tenant traffic (slice A) to overlay; monitor every 60s for errors and tail latency
C) Canary wave 2 (T+30m): if wave 1 OK, shift additional 20% (slice B); continue monitor
D) Full staging (T+60m): expand to 60% and run regression tests; if steady for 30m -> promote to rollout window

Rollback triggers (absolutely abort if any):
- Repeated 504s exceeding 0.5% of requests for 5m window
- p95 regression >20% sustained for 10m
- Health probe failures > 2 instances across independent AZs

I'll add the traceroute/check scripts to the Confluence page and instrument a short runbook task list for SRE to execute on abort.

Jonas
Principal Infra Eng
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Carl Thompson <carl.thompson@DataForge.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2026 15:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On‑prem VPC fabric — service‑layer overlay validation & rollback plan

Quick security/compliance note:
- Ensure audit logging is enabled on the NVA for the canary window and logs are forwarded to our tenant‑scoped SIEM (we need the log retention to meet our standard 90d for this account).
- If route fallback requires key material rotation, coordinate with Security (kms-ops) ahead of the cutover; we cannot have a rotation in the middle of a canary that affects token decryption.

Also adding one operational ask: include an explicit step to validate the egress proofing (no direct S3/Internet on the canary slices) — we saw a misconfiguration in a past private deploy where a sidecar leaked egress.

Kimberly
Head of Security Ops

I've bumped the runbook version to v1.2 and attached the updated diagram (minor label changes on the proxy adjacencies). Can we take a short 30m dry‑run on Monday 07:30–08:00 PDT to exercise the pre‑canary checks? If yes, I'll schedule with SRE and DataForge and lock the SPOCs.

Thanks — Tessa
